in_cover: Mid-1980s, a lone executive seen from behind stands in a dim Silicon Valley office at dusk, holding a single ceramic memory chip between two fingers. On the desk, a tray of black memory chips sits pushed aside, while a larger square processor chip rests under a desk lamp. Beige computer terminal glowing softly. A mood of a hard goodbye. Cinematic editorial photograph, natural light, shallow depth of field, slightly muted colours. No faces visible, no logos, no readable text.
in_intro: Early 1980s, a clean room in a California chip factory: workers in white bunny suits and hoods seen from behind, pale yellow light, racks of round silicon wafers in plastic carriers. In the foreground, a gloved hand holds a small black chip with gold legs. A sense of a proud young industry. Cinematic editorial photograph, natural light, shallow depth of field, slightly muted colours. No faces visible, no logos, no readable text.
